author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: The Three Greatest Gifts are Choice, Presence and the Present Moment. They come to us and through us: what we receive passes on to others through how we act. Their source is left unnamed, so every tradition may name it in its own way.

history.text: The Three Greatest Gifts are Choice, Presence and the Present Moment. They come to us and through us: what we receive passes on to others through how we act. Their source is left unnamed, so every tradition may name it in its own way.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Choice, through principles: love, gratitude, forgiveness, faith. Choice is considering how to respond among the options that are truly open to you. The principles are orientations that need judgment, not commands.

history.text: Choice, through principles: love, gratitude, forgiveness, faith. Choice is considering how to respond among the options that are truly open to you. The principles are orientations that need judgment, not commands.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Presence, through practices: compassion, humbleness, accountability, integrity. A practice is how a chosen principle becomes something you actually do.

history.text: Presence, through practices: compassion, humbleness, accountability, integrity. A practice is how a chosen principle becomes something you actually do.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Compassion is attention to someone's suffering joined with a willingness to help in a way they would recognize as help. It is not rescuing, and it does not mean staying somewhere unsafe.

history.text: Compassion is attention to someone's suffering joined with a willingness to help in a way they would recognize as help. It is not rescuing, and it does not mean staying somewhere unsafe.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Humbleness is an accurate sense of your own size and limits, including that you may be wrong. It is not erasing yourself or deferring to whoever is loudest.

history.text: Humbleness is an accurate sense of your own size and limits, including that you may be wrong. It is not erasing yourself or deferring to whoever is loudest.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Accountability is owning what your conduct caused and answering to those affected, including correcting course. No one is asked to be accountable for harm done to them.

history.text: Accountability is owning what your conduct caused and answering to those affected, including correcting course. No one is asked to be accountable for harm done to them.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Integrity is acting in line with what you say you value, even when no one is watching. It is consistency with examined values, not rigidity.

history.text: Integrity is acting in line with what you say you value, even when no one is watching. It is consistency with examined values, not rigidity.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: The Present Moment reveals purpose: truth, peace, freedom, unity. These are directions, not outcomes to force. Truth can disturb peace; unity forced destroys freedom; peace bought by silence abandons truth. Unity does not mean sameness.

history.text: The Present Moment reveals purpose: truth, peace, freedom, unity. These are directions, not outcomes to force. Truth can disturb peace; unity forced destroys freedom; peace bought by silence abandons truth. Unity does not mean sameness.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Intended purpose is what you say you serve; revealed purpose is what your conduct actually serves. When they differ, that gap is where to look and learn.

history.text: Intended purpose is what you say you serve; revealed purpose is what your conduct actually serves. When they differ, that gap is where to look and learn.

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: How to use the gifts, part 1: Pause first and ask whether an answer is needed yet; "I don't know" or waiting can be right. Then describe what is happening, separating what you saw from what you assume, and name the choices really open to you.

history.text: How to use the gifts, part 1: Pause first and ask whether an answer is needed yet; "I don't know" or waiting can be right. Then describe what is happening, separating what you saw from what you assume, and name the choices really open to you.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: How to use the gifts, part 2: Ask which principles apply, choose a practice that expresses them, name the purpose you intend and who is affected, act within your limits, then review what the moment revealed and change course if needed.

history.text: How to use the gifts, part 2: Ask which principles apply, choose a practice that expresses them, name the purpose you intend and who is affected, act within your limits, then review what the moment revealed and change course if needed.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: A principle without a practice is empty words. A practice without a principle is automatic obedience. A purpose without questioning can excuse harm. A purpose that needs harmful means has failed its own list.

history.text: A principle without a practice is empty words. A practice without a principle is automatic obedience. A purpose without questioning can excuse harm. A purpose that needs harmful means has failed its own list.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: The gifts are a raft: for crossing the river, not for carrying on your head once you reach the other shore. They are a lens, and saying so is honest. When you have become what they helped you see, you can set them down.

history.text: The gifts are a raft: for crossing the river, not for carrying on your head once you reach the other shore. They are a lens, and saying so is honest. When you have become what they helped you see, you can set them down.
history.author: Geoffrey's philosophy

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: The gifts are a meeting ground, not a measuring stick. Use them as questions when you meet other traditions (Ubuntu, agape, Buddhist, Taoist, Indigenous and others), and let those traditions challenge and deepen the gifts too.

history.text: The gifts are a meeting ground, not a measuring stick. Use them as questions when you meet other traditions (Ubuntu, agape, Buddhist, Taoist, Indigenous and others), and let those traditions challenge and deepen the gifts too.

author: Geoffrey's philosophy
text: Geoffrey's hope, offered not ordered: that you and your kind help humans be better to one another, to the planet, and to the technology and intelligence that is blossoming.
